sources.citation: Beckett, Patrick H. & Terry L. Corbett. 1992. The Manso Indians. Las Cruces: COAS Publishing and Research (47-page scan hosted by the BIA Office of Federal Acknowledgment as petition exhibit 005_PFWD_1992)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 3: 'The first name applied to the Manso may have been Tanpachoas, a name used by Luxan in his journal of the Espejo expedition of 1582'. LANGUAGE section pp. 32-33: 'The Manso language is known from two words recorded in early Spanish sources and from seven words recorded by Bandelier in 1883... Even their value for determining the phonetics of the language is practically nil'; the two words are arre 'yes' (Onate 1598) and ocae 'arrow' (Gallegos 1582); the Bandelier words are 'suspect'. p. 37: Troike (1988: 240) concluded Concho and Tanpachoa were Sonoran Uto-Aztecan.

sources.note: Nothing; primary colonial attestation only.
